title: TypeScript in Svelte, and the checking the compiler does regardless

videos.script:
The planner is JavaScript, and it is already being checked. {{already}} The Svelte compiler warns about accessibility on every compile. And a tool called svelte-check finds sixty-six type errors in a project with no TypeScript in it.

This lesson brings that number to zero. {{data}} First the data gets a shape, written down once. {{routes}} Then the routes take their types from files SvelteKit writes for each one. {{components}} Then the planner class and the components that had errors.

The last error is a puzzle. {{generic}} It is in a page that has not changed, and the fix is to make the list component generic. After that, a typo in a property name is caught before anybody sees it.

And last, {{runtime}} what types cannot do. They are gone when the program runs, and a value from outside still has to be checked by code that runs.
